correctness.rationale: An exact linear single-jump decomposition gives the coefficient W max(c_k/w_k), with positive c_k. Affine reproduction forces K>=1 with all c_k=w_k/W at equality. The moment-telescoping identity proves the precise sign-pattern necessity; an explicit positive construction with centered mean and variance W proves sufficiency, and inversion proves all equality masses. The exact rational checker passed 1,092 edge profiles and 3,000 irregular-grid instances; no computation is used as an infinite-size proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The isotonic result is for a nonlinear projection constrained by a cyclic partial order, not affine regression on a path. Whittaker-Henderson is a finite-penalty resolvent and its range/variation statements are not a weighted affine projector positive design theorem. The stronger unweighted fixed-affine-space instability in an earlier related record applies to Euclidean-symmetric operators with unweighted variation; it neither rules out nor supplies unimodal weighted designs.

originality.rationale: Published comparisons concern different operators or norms. In particular, cyclic isotonic projection is nonlinear and defined on a different graph, Whittaker-Henderson smoothing acts by a difference-penalty resolvent, and Steidl et al. investigate TV diffusion/wavelets. Cleveland supplies the classical least-squares operator but available full text is limited. No inspected statement implies the constructive inverse-design classification; unindexed equivalents remain possible.

value.rationale: The theorem completely solves a motivated positive-weight stability-design question for global affine least-squares smoothing, including an exact sharp two-input norm, if-and-only-if edge-weight characterization valid on arbitrary irregular grids, explicit construction of every nonexpansive observation-mass allocation, and a precise flat-weight obstruction for paths of length at least four. This is structural feasibility and full design classification rather than a routine coefficient recomputation.
